title: How to Make a Pivot Table With AI (Excel & Google Sheets)
short_title: Pivot tables made easy with AI
description:
Pivot tables look scary, but they're the fastest way to summarize a big spreadsheet. In this video a free AI chatbot walks you through making one, step by step:

- What a pivot table actually does
- The prompt to get exact steps for your data
- Rows, Values and Columns explained simply
- Turning it into a chart
- Recommended / suggested pivot tables
- Getting AI to write a summary for your boss
- Refreshing and checking your totals

Works in Excel and Google Sheets, with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or any free AI chatbot.

Subscribe to Work Hacked for a new work shortcut every week.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#excel #pivottable #AItools

scenes.narration: Pivot tables scare a lot of people. But they're the fastest way to make sense of a big spreadsheet. Today, AI will walk you through one in about a minute.
First, what is a pivot table? It takes hundreds or thousands of rows and turns them into a small summary, like total sales for each region.
Here's our example. Every sale is a row, with the region, the product and the amount. With real data this could be five thousand rows.
Now, instead of guessing, tell the AI what your columns are and what question you want answered.

screen.user: My data has Region in column A, Product in B and Amount in C. I want total sales per region. How do I make a pivot table in Excel?
screen.ai: Select your data, go to Insert, then PivotTable, and click OK. Drag Region to Rows and Amount to Values.

scenes.narration: Follow the steps. Select your data, click Insert, then PivotTable, and press OK.
Then drag the fields into place. Region goes into Rows, and Amount goes into Values. Excel adds them up for you.
And here's the result. Five rows became a clean summary, with a grand total at the bottom. With five thousand rows, it works exactly the same.
You can turn it into a chart in two clicks, so you can see right away which region is winning.
Want more detail? Ask AI how to split it by product too. The answer is simple. Drag Product into Columns.

screen.user: How do I see each product's sales inside each region?
screen.ai: Drag Product into the Columns area. You'll get one column for each product.

scenes.narration: Here's a shortcut. In Excel, Insert then Recommended PivotTables gives you ready-made options. In Google Sheets, the pivot table editor shows suggestions too.
Now the part most people forget. Paste your pivot numbers into the chat, and ask AI to write a short summary for your boss.

screen.user: Sales by region: East 2,000, West 1,550, North 700. Write a 2-line summary for my manager.
screen.ai: East led sales with 2,000, followed by West at 1,550. North is lowest at 700 and may need attention.

scenes.narration: One more thing. When your data changes in Excel, right click the pivot table and choose Refresh. Google Sheets updates on its own.
And always check that the grand total matches the total of your original data. If it doesn't, some rows were left out of your selection.
So, describe your columns, ask your question, follow the steps, and let the pivot table do the work.
